maya: Quick sync — bringing up compact-embed-v2 (int8 per-channel) on the standard holdout. Doing a zero-shot cluster + recall@k smoke. Anyone have bandwidth to sanity-check numbers? :eyes:
sanjay: What baselines are you comparing to? tiny-embed-v1 or beryllium-embed? And which holdout?
maya: baseline = tiny-embed-v1 (fp16), holdout = embed-small-10k (mixed short/long queries). Quick paste of top-level results I saw:```
model,quant,recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,avg_cosine
tiny-embed-v1,fp16,0.752,0.898,0.926,0.42
compact-embed-v2,int8,0.732,0.885,0.913,0.40
```
Note: recall@1 down ~2.0pp, recall@5 down ~1.3pp.
lee: 2pp drop on R@1 for int8 is modest but we should check short queries (<8 tokens) — quantization can skew norms there. Can you dump embedding norm distrib?
maya: putting the quick norm hist and kmeans seeds now. Command I ran (for reproductibility):
```
python tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model compact-embed-v2 \
  --quant int8-perchannel \
  --holdout embed-small-10k \
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,cosine,silhouette \
  --kmeans-k 100 \
  --output /tmp/compact_v2_int8_smoke.json
```
oliver: can you also run silhouette per-cluster and a agg kmeans inertia curve (k in [10,50,100,200])? If clusters collapse we might see lower silhouette and that correlates with R@1 drop.
maya: ran k sweep, quick numbers: silhouette(k=100)=0.18 (vs 0.21 baseline), inertia elbow around k~80. Per-cluster recall@1 shows a tiny tail of clusters with <0.4 recall where noisy short queries concentrate.
eva: attached a small ascii plot — looks like two clusters merged near zero-centroid, short queries sit there. :chart_with_downwards_trend:
```
silhouette by k: 0.20 0.195 0.19 0.185 0.18
recall@1 mean: 0.75 0.74 0.732 0.73 0.728
```
ci-bot: CI:emb-evals/2168901234 compact-embed-v2 int8 smoke — pipeline passed: unit tests ok, eval run finished (exit 0). Artifacts: /ci/artifacts/2168901234/compact_v2_int8_smoke.json
sanjay: two quick hypotheses — 1) quantization rounding reduces separation for short token sequences -> drop in dot-prod; 2) token-wise scale mismatch (embedding norm shift). Can we try symmetric vs asymmetric quant and per-tensor vs per-channel?
maya: started a small ablation: int8-perchannel (A), int8-pertensor (B), int8-affine-asymm (C). Will push results in ~30m. If drop >2.5pp on R@1 we should fallback to int8-perchannel but with 8-bit residuals (hybrid) or keep fp16 for small queries only.
lee: also run a tiny reranking eval (bm25+embed re-rank top 100) — sometimes end-to-end R@1 recovers even if raw recall dips.
oliver: noted — if rerank recovers, product impact small. If not, consider re-tuning quant scales per-layer for the final transform.
maya: thanks all — I'll post the ablation artifacts and flag clusters with <0.5 recall for manual inspect. ping @sanjay @lee if you want the raw dumps. :thumbsup:
